<!-- pr-reviewer: cb874d1a5b61bba3637c1d80139b5565b9d45f62 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (two hardening notes below for the owner to weigh, neither blocking).

## What looks good
- Threading is sound. The listener thread (`crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs`) only moves text over mpsc; every world and History access happens on the UI thread in `State::drain_actions` -> `mcp_host::pump` (`crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs:11`, `state.rs` after the user's own `pending` queue). No flecs handle crosses a thread, so there is no data race.
- Commands stay on the undoable path: `answer_live` (`live.rs:47`) lends the GUI's own `History` to the existing `Server` dispatch and hands it back; `mcp_live` tests and the contributor's hands-on check show Ctrl+Z undoing agent steps. `open_project` is refused live, which closes the unsaved-changes bypass.
- Malformed input: bad JSON gives -32700, invalid UTF-8 is lossily decoded, empty lines are skipped, a dropped client/closed channel is logged and the listener carries on. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new files.
- Shutdown: `Inbox::drop` sets the stop flag and joins (bounded by the 50 ms poll), and `Shell::shutdown` drops it before the renderer. Loopback-only bind, off by default, bad port exits 2.
- Layering holds (ui -> app); no schema/component changes; provenance lines present; decision file in `docs/decisions/`; no `CHANGELOG.md` edit; no dependency, build.rs, scripts or `.github` changes.

## Local results (PR head, already up to date with upstream/main, no conflicts; macOS debug)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | builds |
| app `mcp_live` | 6 passed |
| app `mcp` | 13 passed |
| app `mcp_pick` / `mcp_setup` / `mcp_render` | 2 / 3 / 5 passed |
| ui lib `mcp_live` (from `crates/ui`) | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

## Requested before merge
None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **Browser drive-by.** The socket speaks raw line JSON with no auth. A web page can make a browser send an HTTP POST to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` with a `text/plain` body (no-cors); the headers are rejected as -32700, but the body line is a valid JSON-RPC line and is executed. Tools such as `save_project`, `export_tool_library`, `import_model` and `post` take paths, so a hostile page could act on the open document while the server is on. Cheap fix if wanted: drop the connection when the first line looks like an HTTP request (`GET `/`POST `/`HTTP/`), or add the token you mention. Your call as owner; opt-in and loopback limit the exposure.
2. **Line cap is looser than described.** In `serve_client` (`listen.rs`, the `MAX_LINE` check) the length test runs only after `read_until` returns, and `read_until` returns only on newline, EOF or a 50 ms read timeout. A client streaming bytes continuously with no newline never trips the check, so the buffer can still grow past 16 MiB. Reading through `Read::take(MAX_LINE + 1)` or `fill_buf` chunks would enforce it.
3. A client that stops reading its replies can block the listener thread in `writeln!`, so `Inbox::drop` (join) could wait on it at quit; a write timeout on the stream would bound that.
4. While the window is occluded or minimised `request_redraw` may not draw, so an agent call can wait until the window is visible again. Worth a line in the docs.
5. `shell.rs` (1660 lines) and `state.rs` (3934) were already over ~400 and grow slightly; flagged, not blocking.
6. Not exercised by me: Windows/Linux, the bind-failure path, and the GUI itself (not launched); I relied on the contributor's hands-on report.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: c051ba9d08a8e9991ca644420daf1ca1c947bdd1 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The browser drive-by from the previous review is closed.

**What looks good**
- `listen.rs` checks every line, not only the first: `is_json_rpc_line` (the first non-whitespace byte must be `{` or `[`) runs in `forward()` before anything is queued. A non-JSON line gets -32600 and the connection closes, so no later line on that connection is read.
- Reads are bounded as they happen (`take(MAX_LINE+1)` on `read_until`). Writes time out after 5 s (`set_write_timeout`).
- `a_browser_post_never_reaches_the_app` pins the POST case and also shows a real JSON client is still served afterwards.

**Local results** (merged with current upstream/main, which was already contained, so no conflicts; macOS)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_live` | 7 passed, 0 failed (includes the new browser test) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib mcp_live` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

No `build.rs`, `.github`, script or dependency changes.

**Attack variants I ran** against a live `Inbox::listen`, with a throwaway test I did not commit and have deleted. "Reached app" counts requests the app saw via `inbox.next()`.
| Variant | Reached app | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` with `text/plain` and the JSON body on a later line | 0 | -32600, closed |
| same POST split across 3 writes mid-line | 0 | -32600, closed |
| same POST sent one byte at a time for the first 40 bytes | 0 | -32600, closed |
| `GET /{...}` with JSON in the path | 0 | -32600, closed |
| `OPTIONS` preflight | 0 | -32600, closed |
| leading `\r\n`, spaces and a tab, then the POST | 0 | -32600, closed |
| NUL and binary bytes, then a `{}` line | 0 | -32600, closed |
| TLS ClientHello | 0 | nothing queued; waits for a newline that never comes, no panic |
| valid JSON-RPC line, then the HTTP request | 1 (the valid line only) | the HTTP line was never dispatched |
| bare JSON body (a raw TCP client) | 1 | dispatched, as it should be |
| 40 MiB of `{` with no newline | 0 | server stopped reading after about 17 MiB (the 16 MiB cap) and replied -32700 |

A browser cannot control the first line of its request. It is always `METHOD /path HTTP/1.x`, which starts with a letter. So no body line of a browser request can be dispatched.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- It serves one client at a time. An idle client that connects and sends nothing holds the single session, so a second connect waits. A local process can therefore block an agent's session, though it cannot drive the app. Consider an idle timeout later.
- A client that never sends a newline holds the connection until it hangs up or the 16 MiB cap trips. This is bounded memory and does not reach the app.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
